title: Tortilla Chips 300g

drivers.name: Week after promotion
drivers.evidence: Last promotion was 20% off (x1.27 lift); deeper discounts had higher lift. Noise-adjusted post-promo effect is x0.81, but this week's price is regular, and the prior event was not a heavy discount. No basis to apply the full model uplift.

adjustment.analysis: No events or price changes this week. The classical uplift model suggests a 19% pullback due to the week after a promotion, but the last promotion (2026-04-06) was only 20% off and lifted sales by x1.27, not the deeper discounts seen before. The noise-adjusted average post-promo effect is x0.81, but this week’s price is back to regular (3.83), and the prior promotion was shallow. The baseline already reflects recent trend and seasonality. No driver justifies moving the median. The uplift model’s signal is weak evidence and should not override the baseline.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:

  shelf price: 3.83 (+0.0% vs regular price 3.83)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 123.5 | 5%-95%: 80.5 - 253.1 | 10%-90%: 86.7 - 190.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-29% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
